title: Measured local minima give stronger phase alignment than rounded dates for six selected Kepler dips
abstract: We test six known dips of KIC 8462852 with a timing score across periods from 10 to 700 days. Local minima in Kepler release 25 aperture flux give a maximum score of 35.52 out of 36 near 24.23 days. Three sets of 10,000 random trials use continuous dates, valid exposure times, or fixed event quarters. Their full-search tail fractions are 0.0037, 0.0039 and 0.0053. The published rounded dates give fractions of 0.159 to 0.179. Eight measured-time choices give fractions from 0.0018 to 0.0068. Thus the selected time definition changes the conditional timing evidence. Event selection, gaps, quarter offsets and complex dip shape are not fully modeled by the null tests. One aperture minimum follows a data gap. A three-day window clipped another dip and was widened. The tests do not give a calibrated discovery probability. No new event, planet, physical cause or independent telescope confirmation is established. Code, input hashes, null arrays, figures and separate-scratch repeat steps are included.
